source.text:
Want to use Claude Code without paying for an expensive AI subscription?

Free Claude Code is an open-source project aimed at making AI-assisted coding more affordable.

Get started in 3 steps:

history.event_key: User dissatisfaction with OpenAI's product releases and model competitiveness compared to Claude
history.premise: The author expresses frustration with OpenAI, claiming their current models and app experience lag behind competitors like Claude Code and Opus 5.5.

source.author: TokenGremlin
source.text:
I believe OpenAI is facing a lot of internal difficulties right now. People like me who genuinely love ChatGPT are speaking out in huge numbers, and there's a clear consensus:

DevDay was a disappointment, and that's where it all started. Then Tibo's 28 days didn't include the new model we'd been dreaming of. We got several resets, some minor tweaks that could've easily been covered by regular company updates (after all, most of them are just bug fixes!), all in an attempt to bring the ChatGPT App up to the level Claude Code is already at: a lightweight, smooth, functional app without too many bugs.

Opus 5.5 was a shock. It's available on $20 plans with very generous usage limits. Unfortunately, GPT-6.1 Sol simply can't compete, even though it's a "good" model. Fable 5.2 widened the gap even further, and it's terrifying. And so far, all we're seeing are grayscale tests of the GPT-6.2 models, which are far better than the current ones, but OpenAI simply won't release them. All we get are leaks from users themselves, desperately collecting whatever crumbs they can find.

It's like I love ChatGPT and always end up coming back to it, but I'm starting to realize that it's no longer worth waiting for improvements beyond what I already have in the current app and models. Either I come to terms with "the defeat of my favorite AI," or I completely lose my mind. Oh, and apparently touching grass isn't a solution either.

history.premise: Artificial Analysis released Coding Agent Index v2.1 with upgraded benchmarks, showing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5 leading with scores of 58, while noting a 30x cost variance among high-scoring models.

source.author: ArtificialAnlys
source.text:
Announcing Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v2.1, upgrading FrontierCode and Terminal-Bench. Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5 share the lead at 58

The Coding Agent Index measures models in agent harnesses; v2.1 of the Index upgrades FrontierCode from 1.1 to 2.0 and Terminal-Bench from 4.0 to 4.1.

Upgraded:

➤ FrontierCode-AA 2.0 (replacing FrontierCode v1.1): our implementation of Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0, comprising 132 real-world coding tasks graded on whether a repository maintainer would merge the agent's change

➤ Terminal-Bench 4.1 (replacing Terminal-Bench 4.0): the same 66 tasks, scored with updated verifiers that improve reliability and resistance to reward hacking

Staying in the Index: SWE-Atlas-QnA-AA

Key results:

➤ Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5 share the lead at 58: Claude Fable 5.2 scores 58 at both xhigh and high in Claude Code. Claude Opus 5.5 (max) scores 58 in Claude Code and, paired with GPT-6 Luna High, in Cognition's multi-model harness Devin Fusion CLI. Claude Fable 5.2 (max) scores 56 as more of its attempts hit task time limits. Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max, 56) in Claude Code and Gemini 4 Carbon (high, 55) in Antigravity CLI follow

➤ Index scores are lower in v2.1, driven by the upgrade to FrontierCode-AA 2.0: models score lower by 5 points on average. Codex with GPT-6.1 Terra (max) is the only configuration which didn’t fall between versions, sitting within 1 point of its prior score

➤ Cost per task varies ~30x among configurations scoring 48+: from $1.51 for Codex with GPT-6.1 Sol (max, 52) to $44.22 for Claude Code with Claude Fable 5.2 (max, 56)
